statement: On a valid branch of (canon), the actions listed below satisfy (∂a − k∂v)E ≥ 2Γ. (surplus) Except where explicitly allowed, assume m > 0, radial spreading in the quadratic case, crossing in the linear case, and line avoidance for the quadratic c > 1 estimates. (i) Quadratic freezing: k = 0 is admissible if m ≥ k0/(1 + c) for 0 < c < 1, or m ≥ k0/2 for c ≥ 1. (ii) Quadratic motion: for c ≥ 1, k = (c + 1)/4 is admissible. (iii) At quadratic cost c = 1, without radial spreading and allowing m = 0, k = 1/2 is admissible when d ≤ 1/4. (iv) Linear freezing: k = 0 is admissible if m ≥ k0. For c < 1, it suffices more generally that m ≥ k0 − cν, with m > 0 still required. (v) Linear motion with 0 < m ≤ k0: for c ≥ 1, use k = (1+c)/2; for c < 1 and m ≥ k0/(1+c), use k = c. (vi) Linear motion with 2d ≤ c < 1: k = 1 is admissible for every m ∈ [0, 1], including zero. Crossing is needed only when m > 0. All assertions are stable under sufficiently small errors in their hypotheses and inequalities, with the corresponding additive error in (surplus).
